definition: to select, organize, and present items such as art or information

collocations.example: She was hired to curate an exhibition of modern paintings.
The store offers a carefully curated selection of local goods.

definition: a soft, thick bed covering filled with feathers or synthetic material

collocations.example: She bought a new duvet cover in soft blue cotton.
On cold mornings I love to snuggle under the duvet.

definition: to arrange text and images into a form ready for printing

collocations.example: It took a week to typeset the book for publication.
The report had clean, professionally typeset pages throughout.

definition: to communicate and cooperate with others in order to coordinate work

collocations.example: Her job is to liaise with clients about project deadlines.
A good manager must liaise between departments to avoid confusion.

definition: existing only as an idea or in theory, not as something real

collocations.example: The bank reported the notional amount of its derivatives.
The boundary drawn on the old map is purely notional.

definition: a small, brightly colored bird that catches fish near rivers and lakes

collocations.example: We admired a kingfisher's bright feathers beside the stream.
If you are lucky, you may spot a kingfisher diving for fish.

definition: a period when someone rules a country because the monarch is too young or unable

collocations.example: Several important reforms were passed during the regency.
The council voted to establish a regency for the young prince.

definition: a sum of money collected from several people for a shared purpose

collocations.example: Everyone put money in the kitty for the office party.
By the end of the trip, the kitty ran out quickly.

definition: to collect and arrange information or documents in the correct order

collocations.example: Please collate the documents carefully before the meeting starts.
The survey findings were collated into a single clear report.

definition: a small wild plant with pale yellow flowers that blooms in early spring

collocations.example: Pale primrose flowers covered the edge of the woodland.
The first primroses bloom in spring along this path.

definition: a return to a former state, condition, or type

collocations.example: Investors often expect a reversion to the mean over time.
The lease includes a reversion clause returning the land later.

definition: a very small, active brown bird with a short upright tail

collocations.example: We heard a wren's song echo through the quiet hedge.
A wren darted into the bushes as we approached.

definition: a small bus that carries a limited number of passengers

collocations.example: The hotel offers a minibus to the airport each morning.
The tourists lined up to board the minibus outside.

definition: to separate grain from the rest of a plant by beating it

collocations.example: Farmers once had to thresh the wheat by hand.
The grain was threshed and stored before the winter.

definition: to supervise students during a test or examination to prevent cheating

collocations.example: Two teachers will proctor an exam in the main hall.
Staff must proctor carefully to keep the test fair.

definition: a small worm that attaches to the skin and sucks blood

collocations.collocation: a leech attached to his leg
collocations.example: After the swim, a leech attached to his leg.
The guide showed us how to safely remove the leech.

definition: a soft, white, waxy substance used to make candles and seal containers

collocations.example: These candles are made from scented paraffin wax.
The cheese was coated in paraffin to keep it fresh.
